phrases.notes: هَلْ opens a yes/no question. شَجَرَة is feminine, so we say هَذِهِ not هَذَا.

phrases.en: Yes, this is the family of the Messenger.
phrases.notes: نَعَمْ = yes. أُسْرَة = family. The possessive chain أُسْرَةُ الرَّسُولِ has an unwritten "of" between the words — "family of the Messenger".

phrases.en: Peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
phrases.notes: Said after the Prophet's name — here at the end of Uthman's line.

phrases.en: Peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
phrases.notes: Umar repeats the honorific back — same words, said as a response.

phrases.en: This is the son of Abdullah.
phrases.notes: وَلَد = son/boy. عَبْد اللَّه = "servant of Allah", a very common name. Note how وَلَدُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ stacks two possessive chains: son of [servant of Allah].

phrases.en: And this is his mother, Aminah.
phrases.notes: وَالِدَة = mother. The sentence starts وَهَذِهِ (feminine "and this is") because وَالِدَة is feminine — Arabic matches هَذَا/هَذِهِ to the noun, not the person.

phrases.en: And this is his grandfather, Abdul-Muttalib.
phrases.notes: جَدّ = grandfather. Same possessive ه: جَدُّهُ = his grandfather.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal uncle, al-Abbas.
phrases.notes: عَمّ = paternal uncle (father's brother). Not to be confused with خَال = maternal uncle.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal uncle, Hamzah.
phrases.notes: Same word عَمّ. Notice the sentence pattern repeating — good place to read fast.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal uncle, Abu Talib.
phrases.notes: أَبُو = "father of" in a name. When followed by another word, أَب becomes أَبُو (no tanween on it).

phrases.en: And this is his paternal aunt, Safiyyah.
phrases.notes: عَمَّة = paternal aunt. Feminine of عَمّ, formed with ة. Note هَذِهِ matches it.

phrases.en: And this is his son, al-Qasim.
phrases.notes: ابْن = son. اِبْنُهُ has no ال because the possessive already defines it; القَاسِم keeps its ال because it's a name.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Abdullah.
phrases.notes: Same name as p04, different person — the father and the son are both called Abdullah.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Ibrahim.
phrases.notes: إِبْرَاهِيم = Abraham. Same three-word pattern: وَهَذَا + ابْنُهُ + name.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Fatimah.
phrases.notes: ابْنَة = daughter. Feminine of ابْن, formed with ة. هَذِهِ + ابْنَة + feminine name.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Ruqayyah.
phrases.notes: Same pattern. Read the whole sentence as one beat: وَهَذِهِ ابْنَتُهُ رُقَيَّةُ.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Zaynab.
phrases.notes: زَيْنَب is a feminine name. Note the هَذِهِ / ابْنَة / name agreement — all feminine.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Umm Kulthum.
phrases.notes: أُمّ = "mother of" in a name (like أَبُو = father of). أُمُّ كُلْثُومٍ literally = "mother of Kulthum".
